# Commands

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs_reference.py from the code. Do not edit by hand: run python3 tools/gen_docs_reference.py -->

This page lists every `trials` command with the help text that `trials <command> --help` prints. A script writes the page from the command parsers, so it matches the code of this version.

Each command answers `--help`, and `trials --help` lists them all. A [[backends|backend]] may add commands of its own or replace a general one. The section [With the ROS 2 backend](#with-the-ros-2-backend) lists what the ROS 2 backend changes.

## General commands

These commands exist in every project, whatever its backend.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`trials plan`](#trials-plan) | what a campaign still needs (the planner) |
| [`trials run`](#trials-run) | run the trials a campaign still needs (dry run without --execute) |
| [`trials index`](#trials-index) | the coverage index over the recorded trials |
| [`trials records`](#trials-records) | every trial of an experiment with its campaign, gate, slim bag, analyses, video |
| [`trials exclude`](#trials-exclude) | move a trial out of coverage into the issues folder (bags_issues/ or recordings_issues/), with exclusion.json (its reason) |
| [`trials restore`](#trials-restore) | move an excluded trial back into coverage, keeping its old reason |
| [`trials amend`](#trials-amend) | `correct a recorded factor level in corrections.json; trial_metadata.json is never edited` |
| [`trials reverify`](#trials-reverify) | `run a trial's current verify steps again (reverification.json); a pass lifts an abort that came from a verify step only` |
| [`trials lint`](#trials-lint) | check every declaration against the rules (pytest) |
| [`trials validate`](#trials-validate) | is an experiment ready: check, plan, gate, lint, its tests, dry run |
| [`trials gate`](#trials-gate) | run a T-0 gate checklist by hand |
| [`trials analyze`](#trials-analyze) | run a named analysis over a cohort of bags |
| [`trials check`](#trials-check) | validate one campaign file, or list an experiment's factor space |
| [`trials metadata`](#trials-metadata) | audit the recorded trial metadata against the contract |
| [`trials storage`](#trials-storage) | where this host writes heavy bags |
| [`trials profiles`](#trials-profiles) | the record profiles in force (--list), or one profile's topics or record command |
| [`trials version`](#trials-version) | the code version stamped into trials |
| [`trials ui`](#trials-ui) | the web interface (needs Flask: pip install 'robofacts[ui]') |
| [`trials mcp`](#trials-mcp) | an MCP server over stdio for agents: validate, plan, dry run, coverage, never runs a trial (needs pip install 'robofacts[mcp]') |
| [`trials new`](#trials-new) | a new experiment from the template, or --from a similar one |
| [`trials init`](#trials-init) | a new project: the experiments root with its shared config |
| [`trials tool`](#trials-tool) | run a packaged shell tool (estop.sh, robot_action.sh, and the tools a backend adds) |
| [`trials roots`](#trials-roots) | show how the experiments root and the project root resolve |

### trials plan

```text
usage: trials plan [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--set name=a[,b]]
                   [--include-unverified] [--json] [--schedule] [--limit LIMIT]
                   campaign

The planner: which cells of a campaign are still missing.

positional arguments:
  campaign              campaign YAML

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --set name=a[,b]      override a factor (Hydra-shaped); repeatable
  --include-unverified  count trials whose metadata cannot prove them as coverage
  --json                emit the machine-readable plan
  --schedule            also print the execution order the runner will use (the
                        campaign's `order`: seed, blocks, shuffle)
  --limit LIMIT
```

### trials run

```text
usage: trials run [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--set name=a[,b]]
                  [--include-unverified] [--limit LIMIT]
                  [--bags-root repo|external|PATH] [--execute] [--scratch]
                  [--action CMD] [--label WORD] [--slim] [--no-pause] [--quiet-stack]
                  [--gate-override REASON] [--no-voice] [--keep-going]
                  campaign

Run the trials a campaign still needs.

positional arguments:
  campaign

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --set name=a[,b]
  --include-unverified
  --limit LIMIT         run at most N trials
  --bags-root repo|external|PATH, --recordings-root repo|external|PATH
                        where to WRITE the heavy recordings: 'repo' (default, the
                        experiment's recordings folder), 'external' (storage.yaml's
                        external_dest for the recording host), or a path. Overrides
                        runner.yaml. A symlink is left in the repo, so coverage,
                        slimming and analyses read the recording there while its disk is
                        mounted. With the disk unmounted, `trials plan` and `trials run`
                        stop with an error instead of planning without it.
  --execute             actually run. Without this the runner only prints commands.
  --scratch             run ONE ad-hoc diagnostic trial (a scratch recording) through
                        the campaign's stack, T-0 gate and operator steps. Records to
                        the experiment's scratch folder (bags_scratch/ or
                        recordings_scratch/, as the backend names it, never counted as
                        coverage), skips the verify steps, and takes the campaign's own
                        defaults for its shape (--set still pins factors, --action
                        overrides the command).
  --action CMD          (--scratch only) run this command instead of runner.yaml's
                        action. {factor} placeholders are filled as usual.
  --label WORD          (--scratch only) a word for the recording's name,
                        <stamp>_scratch_<label>. The stamp and de-collision are the
                        runner's own, generated at run time - never pre-type a bag name.
  --slim                (--scratch only) also leave a slim copy, in the scratch slim
                        folder (bags_scratch_slim/ or recordings_scratch_slim/).
                        Campaign trials always slim. Scratch recordings do not, unless
                        asked.
  --no-pause            do not wait for Enter between the T-0 gate and the recorder (the
                        pause exists so the operator can pose the rig (stand the robot
                        up, set its tools) without racing the dwell). A hardware run
                        whose stdin is not a terminal is refused without it, because
                        nobody could type fly. Without a terminal, the operator steps
                        are printed but not waited on.
  --quiet-stack         child process output (stack, aux, recorder) goes only to the run
                        log; the terminal keeps the campaign narrative — gate verdicts,
                        trial status, dwell countdown, verify results. Made for the tmux
                        cockpit, whose log pane already follows the full run log.
  --gate-override REASON
                        proceed past a FAILED T-0 gate. The reason and the failed checks
                        are stamped into trial_metadata.json forever (an escape hatch
                        that is visible, never silent). It never passes a failed [HARD]
                        item or a factor check that did not pass.
  --no-voice            print the spoken cues but send none (sets TRIALS_VOICE=off for
                        this run and its child processes). Cues go to the laptop's voice
                        daemon at TRIALS_VOICE_HOST:TRIALS_VOICE_PORT, default
                        127.0.0.1:47900. See
                        https://lorite.github.io/robofacts/guides/spoken-cues/.
  --keep-going          continue the campaign after a blocked trial (the default stops,
                        because a stack that fails the gate usually fails it again).
                        Automatic for a campaign that names a `gate` factor.
```

### trials index

```text
usage: trials index [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--experiment EXPERIMENT]
                    [--factors FACTORS] [--report REPORT] [--summary] [--no-validate]
                    [--condition-space YAML] [--json]

Cross-experiment trial index and coverage report.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --experiment EXPERIMENT
                        restrict to one experiment
  --factors FACTORS     comma-separated axes (default: from the contract, then
                        discovered)
  --report REPORT       write a markdown report here
  --summary             just list what varies per experiment
  --no-validate         skip contract validation (faster)
  --condition-space YAML
                        coverage of ONE condition across experiments, per level and
                        domain (simulation, hardware), e.g.
                        experiments/common/config/condition_spaces/lighting.yaml
  --json                with --condition-space: print JSON
```

### trials records

```text
usage: trials records [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--campaign CAMPAIGN]
                      [--status {usable,unverified,aborted,quarantined,no-data,scratch,blocked,failed,interrupted,excluded,attempt,excluded-any}]
                      [--where FACTOR=VALUE] [--no-scratch] [--scratch-only] [--json]
                      [--posters] [--stills] [--force]
                      experiment

every trial of an experiment, joined with its campaign, class, gate verdict, slim bag,
run log, analyses and videos (newest first)

positional arguments:
  experiment

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --campaign CAMPAIGN   flown by, or counted by, this campaign
  --status {usable,unverified,aborted,quarantined,no-data,scratch,blocked,failed,interrupted,excluded,attempt,excluded-any}
                        a class (usable, unverified, excluded), the reason of an
                        excluded trial (aborted, quarantined, no-data, scratch), an
                        attempt outcome (blocked, failed, interrupted), attempt for
                        every attempt that left no trial, or excluded-any for everything
                        that does not count
  --where FACTOR=VALUE  one cell (repeatable), the spelling of `trials analyze --where`
  --no-scratch          leave out scratch recordings
  --scratch-only        only scratch recordings
  --json                print JSON instead of the table
  --posters             also make the poster frames the UI's card view shows, for the
                        records listed (ffmpeg, cached under runs/posters/)
  --stills              also make the stills and the camera video of the camera that
                        config/trial_media.yaml declares, for the records listed whose
                        bag records it (needs the backend's reader and cv2, cached under
                        runs/camera/)
  --force               with --stills: make them again even when the cache is current
```

### trials exclude

```text
usage: trials exclude [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] --reason REASON
                      --category {infrastructure,operator,estimator,other} [--by BY]
                      [--evidence PATH]
                      experiment trial

move a trial out of coverage into the issues folder (bags/ -> bags_issues/ or
recordings/ -> recordings_issues/, as the backend names them), its slim copy too, and
write exclusion.json beside each, with the reason. Nothing is deleted.

positional arguments:
  experiment
  trial                 the trial's bag directory name (as `trials records` lists it)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --reason REASON       why it must not count, one or two sentences
  --category {infrastructure,operator,estimator,other}
                        infrastructure (network, power, disk), operator (the trial was
                        not run as planned), estimator (the method under test failed),
                        other
  --by BY               who decided (default: $TRIALS_BY, else the login name)
  --evidence PATH       a file that shows it (a plot, a log), repeatable
```

### trials restore

```text
usage: trials restore [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--reason REASON]
                      [--by BY]
                      experiment trial

move an excluded trial back into coverage (bags_issues/ -> bags/ or recordings_issues/
-> recordings/, as the backend names them). Its exclusion.json stays beside it as
exclusion_restored_<time>.json

positional arguments:
  experiment
  trial                 the trial's bag directory name (as `trials records` lists it)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --reason REASON       why it counts again
  --by BY               who decided (default: $TRIALS_BY, else the login name)
```

### trials amend

```text
usage: trials amend [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] --reason REASON [--by BY]
                    experiment trial FACTOR=LEVEL [FACTOR=LEVEL ...]

correct a recorded factor level: corrections.json beside the bag and its slim copy, read
on top of trial_metadata.json, which is never edited

positional arguments:
  experiment
  trial                 the trial's bag directory name (as `trials records` lists it)
  FACTOR=LEVEL          the true level, which must be one the experiment declares

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --reason REASON       how you know the recorded value is wrong
  --by BY               who decided (default: $TRIALS_BY, else the login name)
```

### trials reverify

```text
usage: trials reverify [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT]
                       [--project-root PROJECT_ROOT] --reason REASON
                       [--campaign CAMPAIGN] [--by BY] [--dry-run]
                       experiment trial

run a recorded trial's CURRENT verify steps again and write reverification.json beside
the bag and its slim copy; a pass lifts an abort that came from a verify step only,
trial_metadata.json is never edited

positional arguments:
  experiment
  trial                 the trial's bag directory name (as `trials records` lists it)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --project-root PROJECT_ROOT
                        the working directory of the runner's commands (default:
                        TRIALS_PROJECT_ROOT, trials.yaml, or the parent of the
                        experiments root)
  --reason REASON       which rule changed and why the verdict is in doubt
  --campaign CAMPAIGN   the campaign (default: the trial's line in runs/attempts.jsonl)
  --by BY               who decided (default: $TRIALS_BY, else the login name)
  --dry-run             print the rendered steps, run nothing, write nothing
```

### trials validate

```text
usage: trials validate [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT]
                       [--skip {check,plan,gate,lint,tests,dry_run}] [-v]
                       target

is this experiment ready for its first trial? check, plan, gate, lint, its tests and a
dry run, one verdict

positional arguments:
  target                an experiment (name or directory) or one campaign YAML

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --skip {check,plan,gate,lint,tests,dry_run}
                        leave out a stage (repeatable)
  -v, --verbose         print the output of every stage, not only of the failed ones
```

### trials gate

```text
usage: trials gate [-h] --checklist CHECKLIST [--var NAME=VALUE] [--only CHECK]
                   [--skip CHECK] [--list] [--validate] [--no-daemon-bounce]
                   [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--concurrency {sequential,concurrent}]
                   [--jobs JOBS]

Run an experiment's pre-flight checks.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --checklist CHECKLIST
                        path to config/preflight_checklist.json
  --var NAME=VALUE      fill ${NAME} placeholders in check arguments (repeatable)
  --only CHECK          run only these checks by name (repeatable)
  --skip CHECK          skip these checks by name (repeatable). For checks that are
                        MEANINGLESS for a given trial, not ones that are inconvenient: a
                        skipped check is reported as skipped and recorded, so a bag
                        always says which gates it was held to.
  --list                show the plan without running anything
  --validate            only verify the checklist is coherent (runs nothing); exit 2 on
                        problems
  --no-daemon-bounce    skip the backend's step before the checks (a middleware daemon
                        restart)
  --timeout TIMEOUT     per-check timeout in seconds (default: 60)
  --concurrency {sequential,concurrent}
                        run the machine checks one after another, or the parallel-safe
                        ones together (default: $TRIALS_PREFLIGHT_CONCURRENCY, else the
                        checklist's 'concurrency', else concurrent)
  --jobs JOBS           at most this many checks at once in concurrent mode (default: 8)
```


### trials ui

```text
usage: trials ui [-h] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT]
                 [--no-auth] [--view-only] [--cache-dir CACHE_DIR]

Experiments control surface: the coverage grid, runs with a confirm step, the analyses

  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
```


## With the ROS 2 backend

A project whose `trials.yaml` says `backend: ros2` has these commands in addition to the general ones, or in place of them.

| Command | Change | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`trials explore`](#trials-explore) | added | bring up one condition's stack with a Foxglove view that may change parameters (dry run without --execute, never coverage) |
| [`trials slim`](#trials-slim) | added | archive slim copies of recorded bags |
| [`trials profiles`](#trials-profiles-with-the-ros-2-backend) | replaced | the record profiles in force (--list), or one profile's topics or record command |
| [`trials tool`](#trials-tool-with-the-ros-2-backend) | same command, other help | run a packaged shell tool (estop.sh, robot_action.sh, and the tools a backend adds) |

### trials explore

The ROS 2 backend adds this command.

```text
usage: trials explore [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--set name=value]
                      [--label WORD] [--minutes MINUTES] [--execute]
                      campaign

Bring up one campaign condition's stack with a Foxglove bridge that may change the
parameters runner.yaml allows. No gate, no recording, no action: never coverage.

positional arguments:
  campaign

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --set name=value      pin a factor (the first level of each sweep is used otherwise)
  --label WORD          a word for the output folder, <stamp>_explore_<label>
  --minutes MINUTES     stop by itself after this long (default: until Ctrl-C)
  --execute             actually launch. Without this it only prints the commands.
```

### trials slim

The ROS 2 backend adds this command.

```text
usage: trials slim [-h] [--experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT] [--experiment EXPERIMENT]
                   [--bag BAG] [--limit LIMIT] [--all] [--list] [--force]
                   [--no-compress] [--copy-if-light]

Keep a slim, transferable copy of every recorded bag.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --experiments-root EXPERIMENTS_ROOT
                        the experiments directory (default: TRIALS_EXPERIMENTS_ROOT,
                        trials.yaml, or the nearest experiments/ directory)
  --experiment EXPERIMENT
                        restrict to one experiment directory name
  --bag BAG             archive exactly this bag directory
  --limit LIMIT         stop after N newly archived bags
  --all                 archive every not-yet-archived bag
  --list                show the plan, change nothing
  --force               re-archive bags already done
  --no-compress         skip zstd compression
  --copy-if-light       copy a bag that has no heavy topics instead of skipping it (used
                        for remote trials, where bags_slim is what comes back)
```

### trials profiles with the ROS 2 backend

The ROS 2 backend replaces the general command.

```text
usage: trials profiles [-h] [--list] [--cf-name CF_NAME] [--output OUTPUT]
                       [--storage STORAGE] [--max-duration-sec MAX_DURATION_SEC]
                       [--compression] [--topics-only] [--run]
                       [profile]

Record profiles in the ROS 2 backend: the topics a slim copy drops, and a profile's
record command.

positional arguments:
  profile               a profile name (omit with --list)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --list                list the profiles in force, their size notes and their files
  --cf-name CF_NAME     default: trials.yaml record_profiles.cf_name, else the adapter's
  --output OUTPUT       bag output directory (-o)
  --storage STORAGE
  --max-duration-sec MAX_DURATION_SEC
  --compression         zstd file compression (light bags are small anyway)
  --topics-only         print just the topic list, one per line
  --run                 execute instead of printing
```

### trials tool with the ROS 2 backend

The command is the general one. Its help differs with the ROS 2 backend.

```text
usage: trials tool <name> [args...]

packaged tools:
  estop.sh
  kill_ros.sh
  robot_action.sh
```
